subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath caches inside plugin hook, plugin skill, and sandbox containment checks as the Windows performance/security tradeoff?
rationale: The original global cache shape is too broad for containment checks, and even operation-local reuse changes when filesystem state is re-read in security-sensitive paths, so automation should not decide that policy alone.

options.title: Accept operation-scoped caches after PR review
options.body: Continue with the linked PR or a narrow replacement that keeps cache lifetime caller-owned, proves stale symlink/junction behavior, and refreshes Windows proof.

options.title: Limit caching to non-containment paths
options.body: Reject caching in plugin and sandbox containment checks and pursue only metadata/discovery hot-path optimizations like the merged manifest-registry subset.

options.title: Pause for a cache-lifetime contract
options.body: Hold the issue until maintainers define the exact cache scope allowed for filesystem boundary checks.

recommendation.title: Accept operation-scoped caches after PR review
recommendation.body: Continue with the linked PR or a narrow replacement that keeps cache lifetime caller-owned, proves stale symlink/junction behavior, and refreshes Windows proof.
